thought_title: Deaf to any Christ who did not truly live, die and rise

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Κωφώθητε οὖν, ὅταν ὑμῖν χωρὶς Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ λαλῇ τις, τοῦ ἐκ γένους Δαυείδ, τοῦ ἐκ Μαρίας, ὃς ἀληθῶς ἐγεννήθη, ἔφαγέν τε καὶ ἔπιεν, ἀληθῶς ἐδιώχθη ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτον, ἀληθῶς ἐσταυρώθη καὶ ἀπέθανεν, βλεπόντων τῶν ἐπουρανίων καὶ ἐπιγείων καὶ ὑποχθονίων. [2] ὃς καὶ ἀληθῶς ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ νεκρῶν. ἐγείραντος αὐτὸν τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ, κατὰ τὸ ὁμοίωμα ὃς καὶ ἡμᾶς τοὺς πιστεύοντας αὐτῷ οὕτως ἐγερεῖ ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, οὗ χωρὶς τὸ ἀληθινὸν ζῆν οὐκ ἔχομεν.
pass_a_gloss: Be deaf, then, whenever anyone speaks to you apart from Jesus Christ, who was of the family of David, who was of Mary, who was truly born, both ate and drank, was truly persecuted under Pontius Pilate, was truly crucified and died, while beings in heaven, on earth, and under the earth were watching; who was also truly raised from the dead, his Father having raised him; according to the likeness of this, his Father will likewise raise us also who believe in him, in Christ Jesus, apart from whom we do not have the true living.
pass_b_english: Go deaf, then, when anyone speaks to you apart from Jesus Christ, of David's line, of Mary, who was truly born, who ate and drank, was truly hounded under Pontius Pilate, was truly crucified and died, while those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth looked on (Philippians 2:10); who was also truly raised from the dead.
His Father raised him. And in just that way his Father will raise us too, we who believe in him (2 Corinthians 4:14), in Christ Jesus. Without him we have no true life.

choices.why: Aorist passive imperative: become deaf, a sharp command; the game draft's 'Go deaf' keeps the bite.
The repeated adverb is the anti-docetic hammer; each instance kept in place.
διώκω = pursue, persecute; 'hounded' keeps the pursuit sense in plain English (owner's game draft).

choices.term: βλεπόντων τῶν ἐπουρανίων καὶ ἐπιγείων καὶ ὑποχθονίων
choices.english: while those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth looked on
choices.why: Genitive absolute with personal plurals (beings watching). Refines the game draft's 'heaven, earth, and the world below' to keep beings as the watchers and the Philippians 2:10 triad.
rejected: while heaven, earth, and the world below looked on (game draft; turns watchers into places)

choices.english: in just that way his Father will raise us too
choices.why: ὁμοίωμα + οὕτως: our resurrection follows the pattern of his.

anf_compare.notes: ANF ('Stop your ears … at variance with Jesus Christ … His Father quickening Him') matches in sense; ANF 'by Christ Jesus' for ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.

bible_refs.note: Triad ἐπουρανίων καὶ ἐπιγείων καὶ καταχθονίων (Ignatius: ὑποχθονίων). Allusion.
ὁ ἐγείρας τὸν κύριον Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἡμᾶς σὺν Ἰησοῦ ἐγερεῖ. Allusion. Lake marks 1 Corinthians 15:12 ff.; recorded in notes.

notes: Span = Trallians 9.1–2 (both sections). Shared English across the five Trallians 9 ids.
Lake apparatus at 9.2: κατὰ τὸ ὁμοίωμα ὃς καί G; L 'qui et secundum similitudinem'; SA perhaps imply ὡς καί. The relative ὃς is anacoluthic; translated for sense (his Father will raise us likewise).
Lake's margin marks I Cor 15:12 ff. at 9.2 (resurrection argument); wording is closer to 2 Corinthians 4:14 (ὁ ἐγείρας … καὶ ἡμᾶς … ἐγερεῖ), which is tagged inline.
τὸ ἀληθινὸν ζῆν: articular infinitive, 'true living/life'.
Owner game draft kept for 9.1 except the watchers clause (see choices).

review.notes: Paragraph [1] matches Trallians 9: Κωφώθητε οὖν, ὅταν ὑμῖν χωρὶς Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ λαλῇ τις through οὗ χωρὶς τὸ ἀληθινὸν ζῆν οὐκ ἔχομεν. Pass A keeps every clause, including ἔφαγέν τε καὶ ἔπιεν as 'both ate and drank', the four ἀληθῶς, βλεπόντων τῶν ἐπουρανίων καὶ ἐπιγείων καὶ ὑποχθονίων as watching beings, and οὐκ ἔχομεν as 'we do not have the true living.' Pass B does not reverse this: 'Go deaf, then, when anyone speaks to you apart from Jesus Christ' and 'Without him we have no true life' preserve command, χωρίς, and the negation; 'His Father raised him' keeps the Father as agent of ἐγείραντος αὐτὸν τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ and ἐγερεῖ ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ. Inline (Philippians 2:10) and (2 Corinthians 4:14) match the supplied allusion notes beside the triad and the raising clause. The anacoluthic κατὰ τὸ ὁμοίωμα ὃς καί is disclosed and rendered for sense in both passes.

Paragraph 1: Greek source matches Ignatius Trallians 9. Pass A and B preserve completeness, negation, agency, modality, doctrine. Scripture citations: Philippians 2:10 correctly alludes to the triad ἐπουρανίων, ἐπιγείων, ὑποχθονίων (note: Ignatius uses ὑποχθονίων vs Philippians' καταχθονίων but still valid allusion); 2 Corinthians 4:14 correctly alludes to resurrection wording (ὁ ἐγείρας … καὶ ἡμᾶς … ἐγερεῖ). Title names the thought: 'Deaf to any Christ who did not truly live, die and rise' reflects the core argument. Notes disclose OCR damage and uncertain readings via variants=null and notes on Lake apparatus, anacoluthon, and margin marks. All checks passed.
